prerequisites: To enroll in specific technology subjects (third year), students must have successfully completed at least 60 ECTS credits from basic training module subjects and common industrial branch module subjects (first and second year).
Prior knowledge acquired in Applied Mechanics and Strength of Materials courses is necessary.
It is highly recommended (practically mandatory) to have passed Applied Mechanics and Strength of Materials.
It is also recommended, though not essential, to have passed Kinematics and Dynamics of Machines.

learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand and apply the fundamentals of Machine Design, in such a way that they enable students for the subsequent application of advanced methods and theories in their professional development in areas of Mechanical Engineering, and also provide them with great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Appropriately apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: qualitatively and quantitatively analyze the problematic situation; propose hypotheses and solutions for solving problems typical of Machine Design, in the field of Mechanical Engineering. Understand and interpret the results.

Express correctly, using appropriate means, the theoretical knowledge, resolution methods, results and inherent aspects of the problems posed by the calculation, construction and testing of machines, within Mechanical Engineering, using the specific vocabulary and terminology of the subject.

Work effectively in a group, integrating capacities and knowledge to formulate ideas, debate proposals and make decisions in the development of works typical of Machine Design and within the field of Mechanical Engineering.

Develop designs, projects and processes in the field of Machine Design, and within the field of Mechanical Engineering. As well as carry out measurements, calculations, studies, reports and other similar works, related to problematic situations that may arise in the field of the specialty.
Know, understand, interpret and correctly apply the legislation, specifications, regulations and mandatory standards in Machine Design, within the field of Mechanical Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Chapter I: An updated and unified introduction to machine design.
Chapter II: Study of the behavior of materials subjected to static loads. Specifically, stress concentrations, failure theories, and fracture mechanics will be studied.
Chapter III: Explanation of classical analysis methods for materials under variable fatigue loads, for both uniaxial and multiaxial stresses.
Chapter IV: Given its widespread current use in mechanical design, a brief overview of the Finite Element Method in the computer-aided mechanical design environment.

Chapter V: Applying the knowledge acquired in previous chapters, as well as in previous courses of the Degree, the design of the main machine elements widely used in mechanical engineering, such as shafts, clutches, brakes, belts, bearings, bolted joints, etc., is addressed.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, evaluation can be continuous or final. Continuous evaluation consists of deliverables (30% weight) and either two partial exams (35% each) or a single final ordinary exam (70% weight). Deliverables must achieve a 'PASS' grade, and a minimum score of 2/10 is required in each exam exercise to average them. To pass, both the deliverables and the exams (partials or final) must be passed independently. Students may expressly waive continuous evaluation one month prior to the end of the teaching period, in which case a single comprehensive written exam will be used for final evaluation. The extraordinary call relies on a single final written exam, also requiring a minimum of 2/10 in each exercise for averaging.
